text:
mira: heads up — observed another short spike pattern from org=acrobi yesterday, ~12s high QPS bursts that bypassed steady-state smoothing. looks like per-key tokens were exhausted but org-level backstop didn't kick quick enough.

samir: saw that in the telemetry too. traces show lots of tiny calls (embed small) from the same key with <100ms spacing. token refill seems too slow to absorb.

alex: are we using token-bucket per-key + leaky org bucket? current config is per-key TB (rate=5rps, burst=50) + org leaky with drain=200rps, leak-burst=500.

mira: yes. problem is short spikes where a single key fires many sub-requests -> it blows the per-key burst then falls back to org bucket, but the fallback has a warmup delay due to our smoothing window.

jess: can we give per-key ephemeral credit from org pool immediately for sub-second spikes? like lend-and-return pattern with tight decay.

kevin: implementation risk: lending straight from org pool means accounting races and potential amplification if many keys spike simultaneously. need a cap and fast reclaiming.

eva: UX ask — product wants a console toggle: "ephemeral crediting: sub-second lend" with knob for max-ms-per-lend and total-concurrent-lends. ops folks could enable per-customer.

samir: propose algorithm sketch: when per-key bucket empty, try micro-loan up to X tokens from org pool if org.available > threshold. micro-loan TTL = 1s; if not used, tokens auto-return. track loans in rate-limiter ledger.

mira: sketch looks good. questions: 1) how to pick X? 2) telemetry hooks? 3) fairness when many keys hit at once?

alex: suggest X = min(0.5 * per-key-burst, 20) as default. telemetry: emit loan-granted, loan-expired, loan-reclaimed counters with loan-id. that should help rollouts.

jess: fairness: add circuit-breaker: if org loan-utilization > 60% stop granting new loans until utilization drops. also per-org max concurrent loans.

kevin: performance: must avoid expensive locks. use atomic counters and epoch-based reclaim. loan ledger should be sharded by org and use per-shard CAS.

eva: console: surface realtime "loan utilization" and sample keys with loans. show history sparkline for last 1m. default off for small customers.

samir: edge case: what if loaned tokens allow a heavy request to finish but cause downstream capacity issues (gpu queue flush)? we should size loan in token-equivalents that map to tokenized cost and also check model-queue depth before granting.

mira: good catch. add model-queue check: if queue > threshold, deny loans. also consider tagging loans "non-sla" so can be preempted by canaries or enterprise tenants.

rate-limiter-bot: applied patch-idea-1723: added ephemeral loan counters to staging. metrics: loan.grant=0, loan.expire=0, org.loan_util=0.12.

alex: next steps: 1) implement micro-loan fast path in limiter (non-blocking, atomic), 2) add telemetry + tags, 3) console UX stub, 4) run rollout on staging with synthetic spike tests.

jess: i'll draft console mockups and a brief help text: "Ephemeral crediting allows short bursts by borrowing from org pool. Use with caution; can affect other keys."

mira: thanks. i'll own the limiter change and coordinate with kevin on performance tests. ping me if you want to pair on the CAS sharding. :thumbsup:

samir: great — schedule a 30m sync tomorrow to review patch and test plan.

kevin: +1, will prepare a microbench (latency, CAS retries) and a failure mode test.

eva: i'll wire the console toggle to feature-flag so we can flip per-org in staging.

mira: perfect — closing the thread for now, moving design doc to the repo after sync.
